title: KPI Fuel Gauge and Roadmap Sprint Heuristics
body:
Purpose:
This sheet is a compact, operational-first tracker meant to help product-ops and launch owners make two quick calls each sprint: 1) Is the product roadmap pace fuelled by adequate signal (KPI trend + QA regressions + infra headroom)? 2) If not, trigger a calibrated slow-roll or contingency.

Scope and intended use:
- Weekly sprint-level view for launches and major experiments (pilot -> GA).
- Combines top-level KPIs (adoption, latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate), readiness signals (QA pass rate, eval regressions), and capacity staff indicators (on-call burden, hiring lag).
- Not a replacement for long-form launch playbooks; use it as the single source to: greenlight next-week sprint commitments, flag stalls, and recommend rollback/hold.

How to read the fuel gauge (single-row summary):
- Fuel = weighted score (0-100) combining: KPI momentum (40%), Quality signals (30%), Capacity buffer (20%), Cost/latency risk (10%).
- Interpretation: 75+ = Full Fuel (proceed), 50-74 = Yellow (soft throttle: reduce exposure by 25-50%), <50 = Red (pause rollout + immediate mitigation plan).

Columns (sheet canonical layout):
- Sprint (YYYY-WW)
- Feature/Experiment (brief)
- Owner (product / eng / ops)
- KPI anchor (primary metric + delta vs last sprint)
- KPI momentum score (0-40) (manual calc: normalized delta)
- QA & eval regressions (pass% / regressions flagged)
- Quality score (0-30)
- Capacity buffer (FTEs available on-call / hiring lag days)
- Capacity score (0-20)
- Cost & latency risk (notes + % token cost delta)
- Risk score (0-10)
- Fuel gauge (0-100)
- Decision (Proceed / Throttle / Pause)
- Action items (owner + short task + ETA)

Sample row (exemplar):
- Sprint: 2026-02
- Feature: Hosted API: streaming buffer rewrite
- Owner: Maya Thompson / EngPlatform / Ops-runbook owner: Connor Liu
- KPI anchor: p50 latency 120ms -> 150ms (+25%)
- KPI momentum score: 22/40 (noticeable latency drift but still stable throughput)
- QA & eval regressions: QA pass 92% (2 small decoding regressions)
- Quality score: 20/30
- Capacity buffer: On-call load +18% (1 L4 engineer out), hiring lag 14 days
- Capacity score: 12/20
- Cost & latency risk: token cost +5% due to longer sequences
- Risk score: 3/10
- Fuel gauge: 60/100
- Decision: Yellow - soft throttle (limit high-cost experimental traffic to 25% of cohort; enable fallback model variant)
- Action items: "Maya: trim default max_tokens -> 400 by 2026-02-04; Connor: enable fallback routing policy by 2026-02-05; Rohit: run 10k eval on trimmed prompts by 2026-02-06"

Heuristics and triage playbook (short):
- If Fuel < 50 (Red):
  * Immediately set traffic cap to pilot cohort (<=5% traffic).
  * Disable experimental features that increase token generation or KV cache pressure.
  * Open a high-priority incident in Slack/#prodops with required owner roster and 2-hour check-ins.
  * Execute rollback plan only after assess-within-6-hours and one safe test pass.
- If Fuel between 50-74 (Yellow):
  * Apply soft throttles: limit cohort size, reduce max_tokens for new requests, enable cheaper quantized candidate for embeddings where possible.
  * Schedule targeted evals for the highest-regression prompt sets and flag for model team.
- If Fuel >=75 (Green):
  * Proceed as planned; keep an eye on leading indicators: 24h latency p95 trend and cost per 1k tokens.

Staffing and ramp considerations (operational rules of thumb):
- For any feature that changes median token length >20% require +0.25 FTE SRE coverage for first 72 hours.
- For dedicated/private deployments with burst capacity toggles, require an ops runbook and a hotline contact (named) before bumped traffic.
- Hiring lag estimate column: track days from recruiter brief to expected earliest contributor start; if >21 days, reduce Fuel score by 5 points.

Contingency checklist (short actionable items):
- On-call runbook link (attach to row via linked_artifacts).
- Canary route and rollback playbook (cheat-sheet commands).
- Fallback model variant id and routing policy (state where to flip).
- Customer comm template (short apology + hit mitigation + ETA).

One-week cadence for product-ops owner:
- Monday: update KPI anchor, QA regressions, and capacity buffer (data owners: analytics, qa, recruiting).
- Tuesday: synthesize Fuel score and draft recommended Decision; pin changes to sheet and notify stakeholders via Slack thread.
- Wednesday: review with eng leads and ops; lock action items and owners.
- Friday: run an after-action snapshot (what changed) and record a quick note: "why did Fuel move +/ - X points".

Open questions and known limitations:
- The weighting in the Fuel calculation is intentionally opinionated; we should A/B the weights across 3 sample launches over next quarter and re-calibrate.
- Some signals (like model QA regressions) still require manual triage. Goal: automate pass/fail ingest from eval harness by end of Q2 2026 (linked: PRODOPS-613).

Appendix: Quick formulas (manual):
- KPI momentum (0-40) = clamp((delta_pct_primary_metric / target_delta_pct) * 40, 0, 40)
- Quality score (0-30) = 30 * pass_rate (where pass_rate in 0..1 adjusted down for open regressions)
- Capacity score (0-20) = 20 * min(1, available_oncall_fte / expected_oncall_needed) - hiring_penalty
- Risk score (0-10) = 10 * (1 - normalized_cost_latency_risk)

Notes & provenance:
- This is a working document modeled after recent pilot retros (see linked artifacts).
- Use conservative defaults for the first two launches using this sheet; escalate to product-ops director before a GA decision if Fuel is Yellow for two consecutive sprints.

Fillers / To-do for owner:
- [ ] Wire analytics delta feed to KPI anchor cell (owner: Rohit Shah, ETA 2026-03-17).
- [ ] Add direct eval harness link for automated regression scores (owner: Maya, ETA 2026-04-01).
- [ ] Run weight sensitivity experiment across three pilots (owner: Ava, start 2026-04-05).
